details.description: API key, database password, and JWT secret are hardcoded in source, risking exposure and abuse.
details.fix_explanation: Load secrets from environment variables with non-sensitive placeholders by default.
details.secure_code_snippet:
THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY = os.environ.get("THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY", "CHANGE_ME_THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY")
DB_PASSWORD = os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD", "CHANGE_ME_DB_PASSWORD")
JWT_SECRET = os.environ.get("JWT_SECRET", "CHANGE_ME_JWT_SECRET")

details.description: User-controlled input is interpolated directly into SQL query strings.
details.fix_explanation: Use parameterized queries with placeholders and pass parameters separately.
details.secure_code_snippet: cursor.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name = ?", (username,))

details.description: SQL queries containing user data are printed to stdout, which may leak sensitive information.
details.fix_explanation: Remove the print or log safely without user data; keep logging minimal.
details.secure_code_snippet:
# removed verbose query logging
cursor.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name = ?", (username,))

details.description: Arbitrary URLs can be fetched, enabling access to internal services or metadata endpoints.
details.fix_explanation: Implement URL allowlist checks and block private/loopback addresses before requesting.

details.description: User input is passed to os.system for tar creation, allowing command injection.
details.fix_explanation: Use Python's tarfile module and validate paths to avoid shell execution.
details.secure_code_snippet:
with tarfile.open(backup_name, "w:gz") as tar:
    tar.add(target_path, arcname=target_path.name)

details.description: load_config falls back to eval on untrusted input.
details.fix_explanation: Replace eval with json.loads first, then ast.literal_eval for safe literal parsing; reject invalid input.

details.description: request.json is accessed without validation, risking None-type errors and potential crashes.
details.fix_explanation: Use request.get_json(silent=True) and validate required fields before use.

details.description: Flask debug mode is always enabled, which can expose the Werkzeug debugger and code execution in production.
details.fix_explanation: Make debug configurable via environment variable; default to False.
